t: That section 11–341 (b) of the District of Columbia Code is amended by striking out “at not more than $6.50 per volume” and inserting in lieu thereof “at not more than $12 per volume”.

fable.w: This section only amends a D.C. Code provision to raise a per-volume price cap from $6.50 to $12. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government, so there is no real tempting reading toward participation.
fable.s: by striking out “at not more than $6.50 per volume” and inserting in lieu thereof “at not more than $12 per volume”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple amendment to a statutory price limit for books or volumes. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation with entities outside the federal government. It is purely a legislative adjustment of a monetary cap.
qwen_block.s: That section 11–341 (b) of the District of Columbia Code is amended by striking out “at not more than $6.50 per volume” and inserting in lieu thereof “at not more than $12 per volume”.

opus.w: The section only changes a price limit in the District of Columbia Code from $6.50 to $12 per volume. It sets up no process for states, experts, the public or other outside parties to be consulted or to take part in a federal decision. Nothing in it even suggests a 'Yes' reading.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking:** This amendment only raises a price cap in the D.C. Code, from $6.50 to $12 per volume. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision, and there is no hearing, comment period, committee, consultation or right to sue. Nothing here even tempts a "Yes" reading.
